blocks.text: Text in double quotes is a **string** (`str`): an immutable view of UTF-8 memory, so it can hold any language. `'A'` in single quotes is a single character and its value is the ASCII number (`u8`).
Special characters are written with `\`: `\n` a new line, `\t` a tab, `\\` a backslash, `\"` a double quote.

blocks.prompt: With a single `print`, output two lines: `One` and `Two`. (use `\n`)

options: No: one is a character, the other a string
blocks.why: Single quotes make a character (a number), double quotes make a string.
